newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anbeeco slides after says talks end.
newsitem.headline: Anbeeco slides after says talks end.

text.p: Shares in watch and clock distributors Anbeeco Investment Holdings Ltd fell sharply in early Tuesday dealings after the firm said that negotiations it had been having had been terminated.
By 0740 GMT Anbeeco shares were down almost 30 percent or 62 cents to 150 cents in brisk volume of 140,000 shares.
"The cautionary was dropped and that is why the guys have hit them down," one dealer said.

Anbeeco said earlier that unspecified negotiations first announced on July 1 had been terminated and it was withdrawing its cautionary announcement. As recent as a week ago, it said these talks were at an advanced stage.
Barry Phillips, Anbeeco's managing director declined to comment on the reason for the talks' suspension.
"What was expressed a week ago was an accurate reflection at the time, but sometimes things take a speed wobble at the last moment," Phillips told Reuters.
"We believe that it was in the interests of shareholders to advise what the current status is," he added.
The company's shares had risen over 30 percent this month on speculation that the talks it was in would strongly benefit the firm, dealers said.
